normative_sections.rationale: RFC 6066 cross-extension transcript and resumption behavior is delegated to the transport handshake-codec requirement and is not claimed by the OCSP certificate-status target.
RFC 6066 terminology is reviewed and dispositioned by the transport section policy; the OCSP bundle delegates that non-behavioral context without claiming coverage.
RFC 6066 SNI behavior is delegated to the ClientHello and authenticated server-flight transport requirements and is not attributed to certificate-status negotiation.

RFC 6066 maximum-fragment-length behavior is delegated to the reviewed transport exclusion, bounded wire-ignore path, and separate configuration-rejection boundary rather than the OCSP implementation target.

RFC 6066 client-certificate-URL behavior is delegated to the reviewed transport exclusion, bounded wire-ignore path, and configuration-rejection boundary, preventing the OCSP target from claiming fetch controls.
RFC 6066 trusted-CA indication is delegated to the reviewed transport exclusion, bounded wire-ignore path, and configuration-rejection boundary and has no certificate-status implementation ownership.
RFC 6066 truncated-HMAC behavior is delegated to the reviewed transport exclusion, bounded wire-ignore path, and configuration-rejection boundary and cannot be laundered through an OCSP target.
RFC 6066 extension-alert behavior is delegated to the shared typed TLS failure requirement; the OCSP bundle does not claim wire-alert implementation coverage.
RFC 6066 PkiPath MIME registration is delegated to the reviewed client-certificate-URL exclusion and configuration-rejection boundary outside certificate-status negotiation.
RFC 6066 SNI security considerations are delegated to the authenticated server-flight transport requirement and cannot appear as OCSP security-control evidence.
RFC 6066 client-certificate-URL security considerations are delegated to the reviewed transport exclusion, bounded wire-ignore path, and configuration-rejection boundary outside the OCSP target.
RFC 6961 section 1.1 defines BCP 14 terminology and conventions rather than an independently implementable OCSP behavior; it remains reviewed context and is not assigned to a requirement.

surfaces.rationale: ML-KEM and hybrid normative population is explicitly owned by v0.3.5 and remains blocked from this classical cryptography pass.
ML-KEM PKIX credential implementation is owned by v0.60.11 after its complete hybrid authority review at v0.3.5.
